routing.label: DEFAULT
routing.text: A worker claims only its pool's subject (commands.<pool>.>); a step reaches a pool through the pool its command is published to. Orchestration of system/* drives runs on the system pool.

slot_model.label: DEFAULT
slot_model.text: A worker process has WORKER_MAX_CONCURRENT slots (a semaphore). A slot is acquired before the worker pulls a command and released when that command's tool returns. A pool's capacity is replicas x slots; commands beyond it queue on the command bus.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Estimate wall clock as steps x per_step_overhead + sum(step work) + hops x hop_overhead, where hops are kind: playbook children. On prod today use ~4.5 s per step and ~9-15 s per hop (orchestration_overhead.measured), and re-measure: the overhead, not the work, decides the total.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Prefer an inline python step to a kind: playbook child when the child only wraps one call: each hop measured ~9-15 s of orchestration on prod, and inlining cut a planner turn by 44%.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Count slots, not steps, for concurrency: a parallel loop dispatches every item at once and max_in_flight does not throttle it, so N items need N free slots on the target pool or the rest queue. The prod user pool has 8 slots at minimum and 80 at maximum; the system pool has 4.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: An awaited child (return_result / return_step) or a hosted agent's playbook tool holds the parent's slot while the child needs another. Budget two slots per awaiting parent and avoid sending both to a small pool.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Bound every loop and back-edge with a when: guard on an explicit counter: the server enforces no iteration cap, and each pass is a full step.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Set timeout_seconds on python, shell, postgres, duckdb and rhai steps that call anything slow: those kinds have no default timeout and the worker has no per-command one.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: For kind: wasm, plan inside the defaults (30 s, 10e9 fuel, 1024 MiB) and expect one module at a time per worker process: concurrent wasm steps on one pod serialize. Read fuel actually spent from the worker's debug log; no metric reports it.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: For kind: agent, the tool-call budget (32) and child timeout (180 s) bound a hosted loop: worst case is about 32 x 180 s = 96 min of one held slot. Size max_turns and the tool list so the expected path uses a few calls, and read agent.final for the real count.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Keep step results under 100 KiB when a downstream step reads them: larger results are spilled to the result store and every read becomes a fetch.

heuristics.label: GUIDANCE
heuristics.rule: Choose a pool by where the work must run (credentials, network, memory) first; then check its slot capacity against the plan's peak parallelism. Bursts above capacity on the user pool trigger KEDA scale-up, which can add node provisioning time (~60-90 s) on Autopilot.

heuristics.label: TARGET
heuristics.rule: Orchestrator-driven resume of a hosted agent loop after a worker dies (today the step restarts from turn 1).

orchestration_overhead.summary: Each step pays a fixed orchestration cost (command dispatch, claim, and three lifecycle event emits) on top of its work; each kind: playbook hop pays a whole child execution's worth.

purpose: Plan a playbook's time, slots, fuel, memory and tool calls before running it, then measure the run and refine.
read_first: Latency on NoETL is dominated by orchestration per step, not by the work a step does. Count steps and sub-playbook hops before estimating anything else.
Measurements are dated and environment-specific. A figure from kind does not transfer to prod, and an older figure may predate a fix.
Live values beat this file: a running server answers /api/dsl/version; a running worker's limits are its env; actual cost is in the events and metrics listed under metrics.

no_global_timeout.label: DEFAULT
no_global_timeout.text: The worker sets no wall-clock timeout per command. A step is bounded only by its own tool's timeout; kinds listed with timeout none can hold a slot indefinitely unless the step sets one.

retry_config_inert.label: DEFAULT
retry_config_inert.text: ToolConfig.retry (max_retries 3, 500 ms initial, x2, 10 s max) is parsed but no executor applies it; do not budget for automatic tool retries.

slot_rule.label: DEFAULT
slot_rule.source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/worker.rs:748-754, 848-897 (permit moved into the spawned task)
slot_rule.text: Every command holds one worker slot from claim until its tool returns, including case evaluation and its lifecycle event emits; a slot is released early only on a failed or refused claim. Waiting inside a tool (an awaited sub-playbook, a polled Kubernetes Job, an LLM call) keeps the slot.
